summary: With a few minutes left I added the one piece that makes the finding actionable from what the investigation already read, rather than new execution: a detection note. GetConfiguration and Stats expose the node's in-memory configuration and its index (api.go 1231-1237 plus the accessor), so the state is found by comparing that configuration against a peer's or against the newest configuration entry in the node's own store — not by any threshold on indexes — with the two observed forms being an empty in-memory configuration (zero servers and zero peers while the log is complete) and a configuration older than the newest configuration entry in that node's log (two servers where peers report three or four). The note also warns off the obvious false positive: latest_configuration_index below commit_index is normal, because a configuration entry remains the latest while ordinary entries keep committing, so that comparison alone does not indicate this state. Earlier in the run I corrected an over-broad claim in a durable entry after re-reading the snapshot trigger and the user-restore hole, recorded a merge artifact in another entry's evidence list instead of working around it silently, and verified by hashing that every current harness in the draft is byte-identical to its executed revision. The account stands complete with no open gaps and the budget at its end.
